Mississaugas of Scugog Island First Nation

The Mississaugas of Scugog Island First Nation’s own history connects life around Lake Scugog with displacement and return. A dated infrastructure announcement offers another starting point into community priorities.

01

A community account of land loss and return

The Nation describes seasonal work around Lake Scugog and the pressures of settlement, logging and dams. Its account follows Chief Jacob Crane’s community through Balsam Lake and a return to Scugog, where annuity funds helped repurchase land. This is the Nation’s historical interpretation, with original records still to examine.

Read the sources [1] Mississaugas of Scugog Island First Nation

02

Read infrastructure announcements in their own time

In August2017, Canada announced support for a treatment plant, distribution and fire protection. Chief Kelly LaRocca described what the planned plant would mean for members. This record shows community and government priorities at that time; it does not establish completion or today’s water conditions.

Origin & History ↗

The Nation’s public account links seasonal land use, displacement and return. Its interpretation is attributed; original land, treaty and family records were not inspected.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Complete substantive main body, web lines39–73, especially Origins and Land Loss and Return. First Nation historical interpretation; no author or publication date stated.

Review recorded: October 28, 2026

Access note: Actual selected public content read without an account or challenge. Underlying records, historical linguistic accounts and legal instruments uninspected; no current boundary or legal conclusion.

Publication: 2017-08-15

A dated funding announcement with the Chief’s prospective statement about a treatment plant, distribution and fire protection. It does not prove construction completion or current drinking-water safety.

Scope: Complete substantive news-release body and quotations, web lines28–47; dated August15,2017. Government announcement containing an attributed First Nation Chief statement.
